baseline.versionPolicy: Stable outcomes apply across supported Android releases; verify lifecycle, permission, storage, build, and Jetpack mechanisms against the repository-pinned toolchain.

owns: optional business use cases and invariants

hardOutcomes: Durable facts and state transitions have explicit owners and conflict rules.
Gradle and source dependencies are acyclic.
Longer-lived objects never retain shorter-lived UI owners unsafely.

invariants.outcome: Gradle and source dependencies are acyclic, and durable facts, shared state, navigation effects, and asynchronous work have explicit owners.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Single- or multi-module layouts qualify when dependency evidence and mutation paths prove the same ownership, direction, and absence of cycles.

invariants.outcome: Every adopted exported component, deep link, WebView, file, network, credential, and external-input boundary enforces least privilege, authorization, ownership, and platform security controls.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Different navigation and security mechanisms comply when manifest inspection and negative tests prove equivalent validation, isolation, secure transport, and non-disclosure.

invariants.outcome: Actual UI state, critical input, asynchronous work, and resources obey their declared lifecycle and process-death boundary without loss, duplicate effects, leaked owners, or main-thread blocking.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Saved state, persistent storage, WorkManager, or another mechanism qualifies when recreation and cancellation tests prove the required durability and at-least-once behavior.

invariants.outcome: Persistent data has a unique owner, an explicit conflict policy, and a tested non-destructive migration path across every supported upgrade window.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Room or another storage layer complies when schema history and upgrade tests protect the same data and compatibility guarantees without production destructive fallback.

invariants.outcome: Every supported build variant, including the production artifact, resolves declared inputs and repeatably passes compilation, shrinking, signing preparation, lint, and risk-relevant tests from a clean checkout.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any Gradle topology qualifies when clean builds bind the actual variant, dependencies, resources, generated inputs, shrinker rules, and artifact without personal-machine state.

proves: The declared production assembly task creates its artifact with the active pinned toolchain.
doesNotProve: Signing custody, runtime behavior, or every reflection path survives shrinking.

proves: Configured Android lint checks pass for the selected variant set.
doesNotProve: Runtime authorization, tenant ownership, or process-death recovery is correct.

proves: The repository-selected Android tests pass for exercised variants and behavior.
doesNotProve: Unselected devices, API levels, lifecycle races, and production-only paths are correct.

scenarios.failure: A user upgrades across a supported version gap and schema opening crashes or silently destroys authoritative local data.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Run migration tests from every supported starting schema through the production path and verify preserved facts and constraints.

scenarios.failure: An exported entry or untrusted WebView value bypasses type, permission, path, URL, actor, or resource-ownership validation.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Enumerate the effective exported and WebView attack surface and exercise malformed, unauthorized, cross-account, and hostile-origin inputs.

scenarios.failure: The system kills the process after critical user input or work scheduling, causing data loss, duplicate submission, or restoration from stale in-memory state.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Recreate the process and relevant navigation state, then prove critical inputs restore and effects resume or deduplicate according to the declared delivery contract.
